notes:
POC launched (Nov 2025) for commuter chat assistant + schedule reranking. Initial promise: reduce call center volume by 18% and speed up miss-trip lookup. POC scope: 3 endpoints (chat, rerank API, embeddings for knowledge base). Wet run completed internally 2025-12-09; perf baseline established against their current vendor (ZephyrAI).

Summary of current state (short): POC started but has stalled. Engineering team pulled into fare system upgrade (Jan 2026) → missed integration milestone (Jan 29). Security raised data residency and KMS/HSM questions in Feb; asked for SOC2 + iso27001 evidence and an on-prem audit plan. Procurement then put all AI spend on hold (Feb 10) citing budget freeze. Decision: account effectively stalled; competing pilot from Routesense showed lower integration effort (edge + managed connectors) and Saltmarsh procurement is favoring the lower-risk path.

Quotes from contacts: "We like Redwood's latency numbers, but we can't reassign engs until the fare rollout is done." — Nadia Ortiz (Head of Product). "Procurement froze all cloud pilots until Q3 budget review." — CFO (via procurement mail).

What we delivered: baseline throughput/latency reports, small sandbox deployment in their VPC (sandbox), prompt eval deck, and a short demo of fallback routing. Open items delivered to customer drive: pricing scenario, security FAQ, PoC runbook.

Why it stalled: mixture of internal prioritization (no cycles), procurement/budget freeze, and security wanting an on-prem audit which they don't have resources to schedule. Also lost some momentum after the head of product left in late Jan — no clear champion to push the POC across finish line.

Win back signal: if procurement re-opens small pilots in July or if the new Head of Product prioritizes support cost reduction. Suggested short-term tactic: propose a 4-week bridging pilot with limited scope (chat only), discounted dedicated capacity, and a focused security Q&A with Redwood's compliance team.
